title: Stock Market Today Highlights, October 28: Sensex declines 353 points dragged by Reliance, IT stocks, rising crude oil prices - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 352.64 points, or 0.48%, to settle at 73,246.03, recovering most of its sharp intraday losses. The 50-share NSE Nifty was down 50.90 points, or 0.22%, to end at 22,698.85.

Shares of Jio Platforms, the Reliance Industries-backed digital services company, made a blockbuster debut on Wednesday. The stock ended nearly 27% higher against the issue price of ₹1,119, becoming the second most valuable domestic firm after Reliance Industries by market capitalisation. Jio Platforms commanded a market valuation of ₹13 lakh crore.

From the 30 Sensex firms, Reliance Industries dropped 3.46%, Infosys 3.34%, Tech Mahindra 1.83%, Tata Consultancy Services 1.68%, Bharti Airtel 1.42% and Tata Steel 1.37%. Trent, State Bank of India, Axis Bank and InterGlobe Aviation were also the winners from the blue-chip pack.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, jumped 0.99% to $114.5 per barrel.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹4,240.39 crore on Tuesday, according to exchange data.

In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 95.01 against the dollar, then lost ground to touch an intra-day low of 95.29 and finally settled for the day at 95.28 (provisional), registering a decline of 21 paise over its previous close.

SEBI will review foreign portfolio investor compliance norms and seek views on aligning Indian rules with global standards while retaining investor safeguards.

JSW Greentech wins a JSW Cement order for 100 AMPSTAR electric 55T 4x2 tractor trucks with battery-swapping BaaS and road-ready certification.

APSEZ posts 16.5% quarterly profit rise amid 24% revenue growth across ports, logistics, and marine segments; strong international expansion and higher guidance.

SEBI is implementing a global AI supervisory toolkit and exploring a domestic AI model while reviewing foreign investor compliance rules for global alignment.

TVS Credit Services Limited, part of TVS VENU and one of India’s leading NBFCs, announced its financial results today for the quarter and half-year ended 30 September 2026.

The Company registered a 31% growth in disbursements in Q2 FY27 compared to Q2 FY26. TVS Credit reported a Total Income of Rs. 2,029 crores for Q2 FY27, a growth of 14% from Q2 FY26, and a Profit after Tax of Rs. 243 crores for Q2 FY27, a growth of 19% compared to the same period last year.

Equirus Securities, the Institutional Equities arm of the Equirus Group, today announced key leadership elevations within its Institutional Equities business, with Maulik Patel elevated as Head of Equities, alongside the appointments of Harshit Patel as Co-Head of Research and Viral Desai as Co-Head of Sales.

Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company Limited (“KMAMC”/“Kotak Mutual Fund”) announced the launch of the Kotak Nifty Realty Index Fund, an open-ended scheme that seeks to replicate and track the Nifty Realty Index, subject to tracking error. The New Fund Offer (NFO) opened on 26 October 2026 and closes on 9 November 2026.

India’s real estate sector is benefiting from structural shifts including urbanisation, rising incomes, infrastructure development and increasing formalisation under frameworks such as the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA). The opportunity spans residential, commercial, retail, hospitality and industrial warehousing segments.

The Kotak Nifty Realty Index Fund offers investors an opportunity to participate in India’s listed real estate sector through a passive investment strategy linked to the Nifty Realty Index. As on 30th Sep 2026, The index comprises 10 NSE-listed real estate stocks and is rebalanced semi-annually.

Oil prices rose more than 1% after an attack on a major Saudi Arabia refinery by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Tuesday renewed supply concerns.

Tata Projects has secured a GSFC contract to build an integrated acid complex at Sikka, Gujarat, featuring phosphoric and sulphuric acid plants.

Hyundai India posts a 24% quarterly profit drop amid rising material costs, despite higher revenue and resilient demand.

Jain Irrigation has signed a deal with Supercritical for up to 19,000 tonnes of biochar credits as demand rises and global supplies tighten.

City Union Bank posts 26% Q2 net rise to ₹416 crore, with 27% interest income growth to ₹2,092 crore and NPA at 0.48%.

Vedanta posts a 9.11% quarterly profit rise as base metal prices, especially zinc and copper, lift revenue and margins.

India's Cabinet has approved a ₹10,000-crore shipping container manufacturing programme amid global conflicts disrupting maritime trade and container availability.

JSW Energy reported standalone PAT of Rs 261.21 crore in Q2FY27 compared to Rs 190.17 crore in Q2FY26.

Board approved raising long term funds up to Rs. 5,000 crore through issuance of NCDs.

PVR INOX posts over double Q2 profit on strong box office, higher ticket sales, and expanding occupancy.

Indian stocks may rebound in November as the Nifty enters oversold territory, but high crude oil prices and global AI bets could limit gains.

On a quarterly basis the company reported nearly 3% growth in profit attributable to company owners and revenue grew 1% compared to previous quarter

TVS Motor Company’s standalone PAT soared 52.4% to ₹1,377.15 crore in Q2FY27 against ₹903.64 crore in Q2FY26.

Board approved acquisition of entire stake of Harita ARC; and entire stake of STPL Trading and Services Private Limited (“STPL”) for a sum of ₹530.08 crore.

Shares traded 4% higher at ₹4,254.90 on the NSE.

The Karnataka Bank reported standalone net profit of ₹435.89 crore in Q2FY27 compared to ₹319.12 crore in Q2FY26.

Shares surged 3.5% to ₹310.60 on the NSE.
